key_insight: Anticorrosion performance depends on technology-specific failure mechanisms, not coating thickness alone.
engineering_relevance: Coating selection for austenitic stainless-steel energy equipment should match interface integrity, defect structure, and protective-element reserves to expected corrosion and thermal loads.
method: Comparatively review eight technologies spanning electrodeposition, spraying, laser cladding, diffusion, vapor deposition, and sol-gel processing.
Assess interfaces, defects, phases, protective oxides, service stability, and production material and energy flows.
Classify coatings as defect-controlled, porosity-controlled, diffusion-reserve, metallurgically bound, or reaction-converted systems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a qualitative comparative synthesis identifying distinct performance controls and environmental flows, but provides no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: Environmental rankings require a common functional unit and consistent life-cycle boundaries; the abstract does not establish a universally preferred technology.
paper_title: COMPARATIVE EVALUATION OF TECHNOLOGIES FOR FORMING ANTICORROSION COATINGS ON AUSTENITIC STAINLESS STEELS FOR ENERGY EQUIPMENT BASED ON OPERATIONAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL CRITERIA
